m130: Which photos and videos can I import?
m131: SD Card Import recognizes common RAW, JPEG, and video formats. The scan also shows camera metadata sidecars and unsupported files, so you can review what is on the card. See the {0}guide{/0} for the full workflow.
m132: What happens if I import the same card again?
m133: SD Card Import recognizes files recorded in its import history and skips repeat copies. The review shows what’s new and what’s already imported before you begin.
m135: Into the destination folders you choose. You can keep photos and videos together, use separate destinations, and organize by capture date. Review the planned paths before copying.
m136: Does SD Card Import delete anything from my card?
m137: SD Card Import copies your media without automatically deleting the originals from the source card. When the import finishes, you can safely eject a supported removable card.
m138: How much does SD Card Import cost?
m139: Unlimited completed imports are free for 14 days. After that, a one-time $9.99 U.S. purchase unlocks lifetime access and supports Family Sharing. Scanning and previewing stay free. Local pricing may vary. The trial does not renew or charge automatically; there is no subscription.
m140: What do I need to get started?
m141: A Mac running macOS 14 or newer, a mounted card or source folder, and enough destination space. The {0}install guide{/0} walks you through setup.

m253: How SD Card Import stores data locally and handles diagnostics, updates, and purchases.
m255: Last updated: 2026-09-30. This policy covers SD Card Import, a macOS app for copying photos and videos from SD cards or selected source folders.
m257: SD Card Import stores settings, folder permissions, import history, and duplicate-detection records locally on your Mac. It uses an App Group container shared with its card-detection helper and may also store preferences through macOS UserDefaults.
m259: If you enable portable import receipts, the app creates or appends {0} on writable sources. The hidden ledger contains versioned file fingerprints, relative source paths, sizes, modification and import timestamps, and validation checksums so another Mac can avoid duplicate imports. It does not contain destination paths, usernames, or media contents. The option is disabled by default, read-only sources continue without writing portable history, and ledger access refuses symbolic-link redirection outside the selected source.
m261: Apple handles App Store downloads, updates, and StoreKit purchases. Opening website links or feedback uses your browser or email app. SD Card Import does not upload your media.
m263: Apple processes purchases and restores for SD Card Import. The app uses verified StoreKit transaction and entitlement information to determine whether the 14-day trial or lifetime access is active. Trial timing comes from the verified transaction date. We do not receive payment card details.
m265: SD Card Import does not automatically send analytics, telemetry, import history, media, folder listings, or crash reports to the maintainer. Diagnostics are exported only when you request them and may contain folder names, paths, and error text. Review and redact them before sharing. The app cannot browse system crash reports.
m267: When you email support, you choose which message and attachments to share through your email provider. Public GitHub issues are visible to everyone. Do not attach private photos, videos, full card dumps, credentials, or unredacted logs to public issues.
